title: Descent in the bottom supported degree of a smooth pair
statement:
Use the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], for arbitrary $n\geq1$. Let $V\to B$ be smooth of a fixed finite relative dimension [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to B$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let it have pure codimension $c\geq0$ in the sense of [def-pur-frame-class]: $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ for every $z\in Z$, with Krull dimension the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals. Let $e:U\to V$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and suppose the ideal of $Z_U=Z\times_V U$ in $U$ is generated by $c$ global functions, as for a frame in [def-pur-frame-class]. Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$. On the small etale site of $U$, let $\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}$ be the subsheaf-of-sections functor with support and let $R\underline\Gamma_{Z_U}$ be its right derived functor (these sheaves live on $U$ and vanish off $Z_U$). Write $\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))$ for its cohomology sheaves. Then
$$\mathcal H^b_{Z_U}(A(r))=0\quad(b<2c).$$
The canonical local-to-global edge map identifies
$$H^{2c}_{Z_U\times_U W}(W,A(r))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma\bigl(W,\mathcal H^{2c}_{Z_U}(A(r))|_W\bigr)$$
for every etale $W\to U$, naturally under further etale restriction. Here the left side is [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The same assertion about the left side holds when it is computed on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, using its canonical comparison with ordinary etale supported cohomology. Consequently, if two classes in $H^{2c}_{Z_U}(U,A(r))$ have equal restrictions on every member of an etale covering of $U$, they are equal. No identification of the degree-$2c$ sheaf with a constant or twist sheaf, and no frame class or orientation, is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support: sheaf supported functor and local-to-global spectral sequence. Lower-degree vanishing is an agent-formulated relative smooth-pair refinement: use etale coordinates of Tag 0FUE (more-morphisms.tex) and the coordinate zero-section calculation of the affine-line route. Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorem 16.7 and Lemma 16.8 explain the analogous smooth-field pair calculation; that field-only theorem is not cited as the relative-base assertion.
